title: sse: fix chunking/framing for partial JSON and token/event ordering
author: Daniel Kim
description: Motivation: We continue to see production incidents and flaky client behaviour when streaming SSE responses that include partial JSON payloads (function/tool calling, structured output) due to incorrect chunk framing and token/event ordering. This manifests as: 1) partial-json fragments split across SSE events without consistent delimiter insertion, 2) token events emitted out-of-order for certain batching paths, and 3) the OpenAI-compatibility proxy occasionally emitting `data: [DONE]` before final JSON close in edge cases. This PR fixes the framing and ordering issues across the serving runtime and the OpenAI compatibility layer. Summary of changes: normalization of in-flight chunk boundaries, deterministic token-event sequencing in the batched path, consistent delimiter insertion for partial JSON outputs, and a compatibility shim that ensures the `data: ` event stream always preserves JSON object token ordering and finalizer semantics. Backwards compatibility: the streaming wire format remains SSE; clients that handled previous partial JSON cases should be unaffected and will see reduced parse errors. Rollout plan: canary to 10% of streaming traffic for 48h, expand to 100% if no regressions. Tests: added unit tests for chunk boundary logic, integration tests against the sse-test harness (including partial-json stress), and an e2e against the OpenAI proxy. Related: references ENG-3421 and SUP-2291 for incident context.
